title: How do we describe the dart throws with four numbers?
description: A table shows how many students needed one to ten throws to hit the centre of a dart board. The students are counted, the smallest and largest values are read off, and the mean and the median come from the frequencies.
teaching_notes: One idea: a frequency table gives the smallest and largest values, the mean from size times frequency, and the median from running totals. Watch for students who take a value with no students as the minimum.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 11)
video_script.why: A child who found a mean and a median from a frequency table now describes a new table with four numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's table of dart throws 1 to 10 with students 1, 0, 0, 1, 4, 9, 12, 15, 10, 10
video_script.anchor: the table of throws from one to ten with the number of students under each
video_script.payoff_line: The mean is about seven point six, and the median is eight

final_answer.spoken: the mean is about seven point six, and the median is eight, with the smallest value one and the largest value ten

maths_rules: minimum: 1 throw has 1 student, so the minimum is 1; maximum: 10 throws has 10 students, so the maximum is 10; 2 and 3 throws have no students
62 values: median = average of the 31st and 32nd; running totals 1, 2, 6, 15, 27, 42; places 28 to 42 hold 8; median = (8 + 8) ÷ 2 = 8
check: 27 students needed 7 or fewer, 15 needed 8, 20 needed more, and 27 + 15 + 20 = 62; places 31 and 32 lie in 28 to 42
video_script.design: One table all video. The students are counted, the first and last filled values are lit, the amounts and their total are written, and a strip of sixty two boxes marks the middle places.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a dart board; a table with throws 1 to 10 in the top row and students 1, 0, 0, 1, 4, 9, 12, 15, 10, 10 in the bottom row

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.board: a dart board appears with the centre circle lit
marks.ask: the words smallest, largest, mean and median appear with empty boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a dart competition.
<bookmark mark='board'/>Each student keeps throwing until the dart hits the centre circle of the board.
<bookmark mark='table'/>The table shows the number of throws from one to ten. Under each is the number of students.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are the smallest value, the largest value, the mean and the median?

beats.on_screen: the table and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: value = number of throws, frequency = number of students; throws 2 and 3 have frequency 0

marks.value: the top row is labelled value and the bottom row frequency
marks.zero: the zeros under 2 and 3 throws are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='value'/>Here the number of throws is the value. The number of students is its frequency.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>A value with no students never occurs in the data.

marks.given: the throws and the number of students are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, throws from one to ten. The students for each are one, zero, zero, one, four, nine, twelve, fifteen, ten and ten.

beats.on_screen: To find: minimum, maximum, mean, median

marks.find: the four words are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the smallest and largest values, the mean and the median.

marks.add: the ten frequencies are lined up

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add the frequencies to count the students.
<bookmark mark='part1'/>One plus zero plus zero plus one plus four is six.
<bookmark mark='part2'/>Six plus nine plus twelve plus fifteen plus ten plus ten is sixty two.

beats.on_screen: smallest value with a student: 1 throw; largest value with a student: 10 throws

marks.min: the column for 1 throw is lit as the minimum
marks.max: the column for 10 throws is lit as the maximum

narration: <bookmark mark='min'/>Step two, find the smallest and largest values. One student needed one throw, so the minimum is one.
<bookmark mark='max'/>Ten students needed ten throws, so the maximum is ten.

marks.mult: each number of throws is multiplied by its students
marks.first: 1, 4, 20, 54 and 84 are written; 2 and 3 are skipped

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, multiply each number of throws by its students.
<bookmark mark='first'/>That gives one, four, twenty, fifty four and eighty four. Two and three add nothing.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Next come one hundred and twenty, ninety and one hundred.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>These add up to four hundred and seventy three throws.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide four hundred and seventy three by sixty two students.

beats.on_screen: 62 values: median = average of the 31st and 32nd; running totals 1, 2, 6, 15, 27, 42; places 28 to 42 hold 8 throws

marks.pos: the 31st and 32nd boxes of a strip of 62 boxes are marked
marks.run: the running totals 1, 2, 6, 15, 27 and 42 are written under 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 throws
marks.both: the boxes from the 28th to the 42nd are lit as 8 throws

narration: <bookmark mark='pos'/>Step four, find the middle places. Sixty two values make the median the average of the thirty first and thirty second.
<bookmark mark='run'/>The running totals are one, two, six, fifteen, twenty seven and forty two.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Places twenty eight to forty two hold eight throws, so both middle values are eight.

beats.on_screen: check: 27 needed 7 or fewer; 15 needed 8; 20 needed more; 27 + 15 + 20 = 62; places 31 and 32 lie among the 15

marks.low: 27 is written under the throws up to 7
marks.mid: 15 is written under 8 throws and 20 under 9 and 10
marks.among: the 31st and 32nd boxes sit inside the lit block of 15

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Check the median. Twenty seven students needed seven throws or fewer.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Fifteen needed eight throws, and twenty needed more than eight.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Twenty seven plus fifteen plus twenty is sixty two.
<bookmark mark='among'/>The middle places fall among the fifteen students who needed eight.

marks.ans: the mean and the median are boxed
marks.range: the minimum and the maximum are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The mean is about seven point six, and the median is eight.
<bookmark mark='range'/>The smallest value is one, and the largest value is ten.
